findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, always false
findings.body: The check for a zero-length override (start equals end) compares two freshly created Dayjs instances with `===`. That is reference equality, so it is never true. As a result, an override that marks the whole day unavailable is not caught by this branch. It should use `.isSame()`.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses slot start for end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same value as `start`. So a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is still accepted. It should use `slotEndTime`. Also, comparing raw UTC hour/minute against minutes-since-midnight working hours does not handle ranges that span midnight. Such ranges can wrongly reject valid slots.

findings.title: Override day skips busy-time check entirely
findings.body: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, the function returns true immediately. It never evaluates `busy`, so existing bookings and calendar events on override days are ignored. That allows double booking. It should fall through to the busy check instead of returning.

findings.title: Multiple overrides on same day reject valid slots
findings.body: `find` returns true as soon as any same-day override excludes the slot. If a user has several override ranges on one day, e.g. 9-10 and 14-15, a slot inside the second range is rejected because it falls outside the first.

findings.title: Slot end not checked against override end
findings.body: Only `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is checked. A slot that starts before the override ends but extends past it is accepted, which allows bookings outside the override window.

findings.title: Override minute-of-day may wrap across midnight
findings.body: Start and end are computed as UTC hour*60+minute after adding the offset. When the shifted time crosses midnight, the end becomes smaller than the start, or lands on a different day. buildSlots then discards the range as invalid, so the override silently yields no slots or the wrong ones. The tests only cover small offsets (+5:30 and +6:00 with an IST organizer).
